purpose: Authoritative backlog of every unresolved question in the agent-first program. This file is the source of truth; docs/AGENTIC_RESEARCH_PROGRAM.md is a generated projection of it. Validated by tests/research-program.test.ts so a forgotten question becomes a failing test rather than an oversight.
notDuplicated: Findings and their reasoning live in docs/AGENTIC_ARCHITECTURE_FORENSIC_AUDIT.md. This file records only status, dependency and next action.

statuses.UNTESTED: No evidence either way. Not blocked, just not attempted.
statuses.PREREGISTERED: Specification committed to config/experiment-registry.json; not yet executed.
statuses.SUPPORTED: Evidence supports the hypothesis under the stated conditions.
statuses.INCONCLUSIVE: Executed; the interval spans the decision boundary. Neither adopted nor refuted.
statuses.BLOCKED: Cannot proceed until a dependency or an external prerequisite resolves.
statuses.DEFERRED: Deliberately postponed on information value, not blocked.
statuses.SUPERSEDED: Replaced by a later item; retained so history stays legible.

stages.name: Semantic architecture
stages.exitCriterion: One DEVELOPMENT architecture has acceptable semantic quality, channel integrity and claim-level auditability, with no clearly superior unresolved architecture immediately adjacent.

stages.name: Inference stability
stages.exitCriterion: The architectural decision and the principal quality conclusions are stable across repeated independent generations, and every KEEP/REJECT threshold has a documented sensitivity range.

stages.name: Semantic construct coverage
stages.exitCriterion: Every product-required construct (E/P/Q/D, uncertainty, contradictions) has defined truth, a defined metric, and a measured implementation.

stages.name: Generalisation
stages.exitCriterion: The frozen architecture passes predefined VALIDATION criteria with no tuning on VALIDATION. Runs once per frozen architecture.

stages.name: Product-realistic evidence
stages.exitCriterion: The architecture works without synthetic pre-routing of evidence and survives realistic ambiguity and contradiction.

stages.name: Human validity
stages.exitCriterion: Real users show acceptable claim correctness, omission and error rates, correction burden, provenance fidelity and recommendation usefulness.

stages.name: Research-to-product integration
stages.exitCriterion: A validated semantic architecture runs in the product path with defined persistence, migration, fallback, latency UX, cost, privacy and security.

stages.name: Agentic expansion
stages.exitCriterion: Each genuinely agentic workflow individually demonstrates value over a simpler deterministic or single-call alternative.

items.question: Can the strongest one-call baseline gain claim-level auditability without specialist inference?
items.evidenceSoFar: Shared blueprint emits no supporting phrase, so its provenance is unmeasurable rather than absent. Isolated Experience achieves 0.000 evidence contamination with a quote; full-context achieves 0.424. Preregistered as person-blueprint-v2:openai:LEXICAL_TRAP:low. Matcher frozen; R-01 is diagnostic only.
items.nextAction: Dry run is green (12 fresh person@v2, 288/288 jobs reused). Paid run only after operator approval.
items.successCriterion: Retrieval holds (CI spans zero or better) AND provenance contamination <= 0.05.
items.latencyRelevance: Small expected increase in output tokens; measure per-call.

items.question: Are the provenance attribution thresholds (0.6 floor, 0.1 ambiguity margin) defensible?
items.evidenceSoFar: Both thresholds are hand-set. Corroborating signal is strong (0 drift, 0 unsupported, 0-1 ambiguous across 500+ claims) but no sensitivity analysis exists.
items.nextAction: Sweep both thresholds over cached outputs and report verdict stability. Deterministic, zero calls.
items.successCriterion: The KEEP/REJECT verdict is unchanged across a documented threshold range.
items.latencyRelevance: None.

items.question: Would we reach the same architectural decision if the model regenerated the same person's blueprint?
items.evidenceSoFar: Nothing known. Every result is one generation per input. Reasoning tokens varied 261-982 at fixed effort, so generation is demonstrably unstable; the score effect is unmeasured.
items.nextAction: Preregister a repeated-generation study: 12 people x 3 fresh trials, trial index in the cache key.
items.successCriterion: The sign of the agent-field-match vs agent-blueprint delta is stable across trials and ranking rank-correlation is high.
items.latencyRelevance: Yields latency variance, currently unknown.

items.question: Does a correctly-scoped Direction Agent beat the shared blueprint on Direction, or only tie it?
items.evidenceSoFar: v2 isolated Direction 0.806 vs shared 0.732, paired delta +0.074 CI [-0.066, 0.198]. Provenance contamination 0.000 and desired volume ratio 1.000, both corrected from v1.
items.nextAction: Resolve at n=24-36 only if P-01 fails and S-01 passes. Deliberately behind both.
items.successCriterion: Direction paired delta CI excludes zero.
items.latencyRelevance: Doubles onboarding calls; requires real concurrent measurement before shipping.

items.question: Do the five non-implications no v1 prompt states change interpretation quality when added?
items.evidenceSoFar: semanticContract.ts records that liked->desired, and all four Qualification rules, are unstated in every v1 prompt. The liked->desired gap is the measured cause of the v1 Direction collapse.
items.nextAction: Define semantic-contract v2 with the full rule set plus contrastive examples, as a new prompt version. Never edit a v1 prompt.
items.successCriterion: No channel regresses and at least one contamination measure improves.
items.latencyRelevance: Longer prompt; measure input-token and latency delta.

items.question: Which of the five semantic role fields carry independent signal, and is the matcher robust to paraphrase?
items.evidenceSoFar: Leave-one-out on the frozen LEXICAL_TRAP OpenAI caches (n=12, 12/12 person and 288/288 job hits). Full field-match experience NDCG@10 0.745. Deltas: action -0.068, object -0.059, method -0.028, domain -0.016, purpose -0.000. Purpose is redundant on this family. Diagnostic only: agent-field-match stays on all five fields for P-01.
items.nextAction: Do not retune the matcher. A later versioned matcher experiment may drop or reweight purpose; that is not P-01.
items.successCriterion: Per-field contribution quantified; any redundant field identified.
items.latencyRelevance: None; deterministic.

items.question: Can an agent extract held qualifications well enough to reproduce the planted meets-requirements/stretch partition?
items.evidenceSoFar: Truth side already exists: frameLabels computes qualificationFeasibility and hardGaps. Blocked because the five planted qualifications per person appear only in the narrative field, which no architecture reads. Per RECOMMENDATION_POLICY this is a partition, never a fourth similarity channel.
items.nextAction: Wait for M-01, which makes qualifications visible as a byproduct of messy narrative rendering.
items.successCriterion: Partition agreement against planted truth, with E/P/D scores byte-identical.
items.latencyRelevance: One extra field on an existing call, or one extra call. Measure.

items.question: Can the representation say 'I do not have enough evidence' instead of inventing a conclusion, and is that signal calibrated?
items.evidenceSoFar: No uncertainty or confidence construct exists anywhere in the schema. Model self-reported confidence must not be assumed calibrated.
items.nextAction: Define the construct before implementing. Candidates: explicit INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE, claim-level evidence strength, repeated-generation agreement as an external proxy.
items.successCriterion: Abstention correlates with actual error; calibration measured before any confidence is shown to a user.
items.latencyRelevance: Minor.

items.question: How should conflicting evidence and user corrections be reconciled?
items.evidenceSoFar: No contradiction handling exists. The corpus contains no contradictory evidence to test against.
items.nextAction: Define source precedence and versioning. Prefer deterministic reconciliation; reserve model adjudication for genuinely ambiguous semantics.
items.successCriterion: A user correction reliably outranks a stale inference while history and provenance are preserved.
items.latencyRelevance: Affects refresh path, not first result.

items.question: Does the frozen architecture generalise to paraphrase families it never saw?
items.evidenceSoFar: VALIDATION has never been used by any agent arm; all four ledger experiment ids are DEVELOPMENT. Elsewhere in this codebase extraction macro F1 drops 0.831 to 0.611 across the boundary.
items.nextAction: Blocked by the architecture-freeze gate. Two of four conditions currently fail.
items.successCriterion: Predefined criteria pass with no tuning on VALIDATION.
items.latencyRelevance: None beyond what DEVELOPMENT already measured.

items.question: Can TaskDNA untangle a messy person, rather than interpret evidence that was already routed for it?
items.evidenceSoFar: The frozen corpus supplies evidence pre-partitioned into three arrays with explicit LIKE/DISLIKE stance and giveaway prefixes such as 'What I liked most:'. Removing the partition inflated full-context Experience volume to 1.736 immediately.
items.nextAction: Requires explicit approval: a new benchmark family is a contract change under amendment C. Same hidden truth, new independent messy-narrative renderer, no channel labels.
items.successCriterion: Channel-assignment accuracy against planted truth, plus retrieval per channel.
items.latencyRelevance: May require a routing step, which would add to the critical path.

items.question: Does the architecture hold for career states the current corpus does not contain?
items.evidenceSoFar: Measured from planted truth: every person has an identical 6/7/2/4 channel profile; desired-vs-performed role overlap is always 2 or 3 of 5; disliked-vs-performed is always exactly 5. No low-experience/high-direction group and no contrast group for direction aversion exist.
items.nextAction: New versioned corpus with its own preregistration. Do not mutate the frozen corpus.
items.successCriterion: Performance holds across pivots, returners, generalists, and qualification/desire mismatches.
items.latencyRelevance: None.

items.question: Are explanations faithful to the evidence and match factors that actually produced the ranking?
items.evidenceSoFar: No explanation generation exists in the agent path. Provenance would make most of this deterministically checkable rather than requiring a model judge.
items.nextAction: Wait for P-01. Then build deterministic explanation validation, not a model critic.
items.successCriterion: Explanation claims trace to evidence the scoring used; zero hallucinated rationale.
items.latencyRelevance: Explanation is post-ranking; affects complete-result time, not first result.

items.question: What is the real user wait when independent calls are actually issued concurrently under provider contention?
items.evidenceSoFar: All parallel figures are derived from individually-timed calls and are optimistically biased lower bounds. Measured: shared 10.8s p50 / 12.0s p95. n=24 puts p95 at the second-largest observation.
items.nextAction: Only meaningful if a multi-call architecture wins. Needs genuine concurrency, >=100 subjects, repeated across times of day.
items.successCriterion: Measured p95 user wait under real concurrency meets a product threshold.
items.latencyRelevance: This item IS the latency question.

items.question: Does JobBlueprint interpretation survive real, noisy job descriptions?
items.evidenceSoFar: Job interpretation works on synthetic renderings. Untested against marketing fluff, duplicated or missing responsibilities, contradictory requirements, title mismatch, jargon, or injected text.
items.nextAction: Assemble a noisy job-description set. Keep interpretation per job and globally cached; never per user-job pair.
items.successCriterion: Structured work recovery holds on noisy input; no injected instruction changes behaviour.
items.latencyRelevance: Precomputed; not user wait.

items.question: Does the architecture separate system instructions from untrusted external data?
items.evidenceSoFar: Evidence is concatenated directly into the prompt with no delimiting or instruction hierarchy. Structured output constrains response shape but not model behaviour. Blast radius is currently small because there are no tools and no external actions.
items.nextAction: Required before ingesting any real content. Explicit data/instruction separation; treat all extracted text as data; never let ingested text reach a tool-calling path.
items.successCriterion: A planted injection in a resume or job description does not alter extraction behaviour.
items.latencyRelevance: None.

items.question: Do real people agree with TaskDNA's representation of their own work?
items.evidenceSoFar: Zero human validity. Everything is planted-truth recovery on synthetic people.
items.nextAction: Design the review program and the privacy prerequisites. Corrections held out under a custodian, never folded into a tuning set.
items.successCriterion: Claim correctness, omission and error rates, and correction burden meet preregistered thresholds.
items.latencyRelevance: Perceived latency becomes measurable here.

items.question: How does a validated semantic architecture replace the deterministic product path?
items.evidenceSoFar: The product runs no model call at all. src/app imports @/domain/engine; nothing under src/app, src/v3 or src/domain imports any agent module. The gap between research and product is total.
items.nextAction: Do not merge research code into the product because DEVELOPMENT metrics look good. Requires persistence, migration, fallback, latency UX, cost, privacy and shadow testing.
items.successCriterion: Shadow-tested parity plus defined SLOs.
items.latencyRelevance: Production UX is decided here.

items.question: Does career-landscape discovery need a genuinely exploratory agent?
items.evidenceSoFar: No tool-using or planning agent exists anywhere in the repository. This is the first component whose task might genuinely require iterative decision-making about what to investigate next.
items.nextAction: Do not implement until the core representation and retrieval foundation are stable.
items.successCriterion: Beats a deterministic or single-call alternative on discovery quality.
items.latencyRelevance: Exploratory loops are latency-expensive by nature.

items.question: Does outreach and opportunity pursuit warrant agentic planning?
items.evidenceSoFar: Networking logic exists as deterministic legacy code and is out of scope for the core matching loop.
items.nextAction: Requires reliable semantic user state, explicit user approval boundaries and narrow tool permissions first.
items.successCriterion: Beats a deterministic plan on user-accepted actions.
items.latencyRelevance: Asynchronous; not on the first-result path.

items.question: Is selective specialist rescue better than always-on specialist inference?
items.evidenceSoFar: Always-on specialists are 0 for 2 on measured wins. A trigger-based hybrid has never been tried.
items.nextAction: Define triggers: ambiguous channel assignment, contradictory evidence, low evidence support, unstable repeated inference.
items.successCriterion: AGENT_RESCUE_RECALL improves without raising AGENT_ONLY_FALSE_DISCOVERY_RATE, at a fraction of always-on cost.
items.latencyRelevance: Only the rescued minority pays the extra call.

items.question: Should the interrupted NATURAL arm be completed?
items.evidenceSoFar: Stopped at 12/12 person and 35/288 job interpretations, all committed. NATURAL is the family where lexical matching already performs well and headroom is smallest (+0.173 to the normaliser control). Partial cache existence is not authorization to finish the arm.
items.nextAction: Do not resume. Revisit only if a regression check on ordinary cases becomes decision-relevant and is newly preregistered. The existing 47 cached calls stay on disk.
items.successCriterion: n/a - a completeness question, not a hypothesis.
items.latencyRelevance: None.
